evidence.claim: The State Department said SOEs and military-owned companies enjoyed significant advantages, many SOEs received tax exemptions, and the December 29, 2022 State Ownership Policy aimed to reduce the government's role and raise private-sector participation from 30 percent to 65 percent.
evidence.title: Egypt - United States Department of State
evidence.excerpt: The State Department said SOEs and military-owned companies enjoyed significant advantages, many SOEs received tax exemptions, and the December 29, 2022 State Ownership Policy aimed to reduce the government's role and raise private-sector participation from 30 percent to 65 percent.
evidence.source_locator: Transparency of the Regulatory System and Privatization Program sections
evidence.source_confidence_reason: U.S. government investment-climate assessment with a direct retrospective description of the 2022 policy baseline.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Describes the structure and policy posture under Sisi's government, including military-linked advantages.
contrary_evidence: This is a 2024 retrospective, not a contemporaneous 2022 report.
The source emphasizes reform needs and thus frames the baseline critically.

evidence.claim: The paper argues that the military spearheaded Sisi's state-led investment strategy, controlled a vast economic portfolio, and benefited from privileged access and opacity that distorted private-sector development.
evidence.title: Retain, Restructure, or Divest? Policy Options for Egypt's Military Economy
evidence.excerpt: The paper argues that the military spearheaded Sisi's state-led investment strategy, controlled a vast economic portfolio, and benefited from privileged access and opacity that distorted private-sector development.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Well-cited policy paper from a major think tank that gives a direct, source-based analysis of Egypt's military economy.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective analysis of the Sisi-era economy that directly covers the 2022 ruler-period context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The paper directly ties the state-led strategy to Sisi's presidency, but the evidence is systemic and network-based rather than a forensic finding of personal enrichment.
contrary_evidence: The same paper notes that some military projects did deliver public works, housing, and logistics benefits.
The same paper notes that some military projects delivered public works, housing, and logistics benefits.

evidence.claim: Sisi appointed Hassan Abdalla as caretaker central bank governor during the currency crisis; Abdalla came from state-owned media leadership and had long banking experience.
evidence.title: Egypt's Sisi names Hassan Abdalla as caretaker cbank head
evidence.excerpt: Sisi appointed Hassan Abdalla as caretaker central bank governor during the currency crisis; Abdalla came from state-owned media leadership and had long banking experience.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-syndicated reporting gives a direct account of the presidential appointment and the appointee's background.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is a direct presidential appointment and therefore attributable to Sisi; the appointee's banking background limits any simple nepotism inference.
contrary_evidence: Abdalla was also described as a veteran banker with relevant experience, so the appointment is not proof of cronyism or incompetence.

evidence.claim: IMF staff and Egyptian authorities agreed on a 46-month EFF package built around macroeconomic stabilization, debt sustainability, a stronger social safety net, and reforms to support private-sector-led growth and job creation.
evidence.title: Egypt: IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement on an Extended Fund Facility Arrangement
evidence.excerpt: IMF staff and Egyptian authorities agreed on a 46-month EFF package built around macroeconomic stabilization, debt sustainability, a stronger social safety net, and reforms to support private-sector-led growth and job creation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct IMF press release announcing the agreed package and its stated policy goals.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Egyptian authorities under Sisi's presidency as the agreed program framework, but it is a commitment rather than proof of execution.
contrary_evidence: The agreement itself does not show that the reforms were fully implemented during 2022.

evidence.claim: The staff report says Egypt's program rests on three pillars: exchange-rate and monetary policy to restore resilience, fiscal discipline to keep debt on a downward path while protecting social spending, and broad structural reforms to reduce the state footprint and level the playing field; it also says the agenda includes publishing a President-endorsed state ownership policy and an ambitious divestment plan.
evidence.title: Arab Republic of Egypt: Request for Extended Arrangement Under the Extended Fund Facility-Press Release; and Staff Report
evidence.excerpt: The staff report says Egypt's program rests on three pillars: exchange-rate and monetary policy to restore resilience, fiscal discipline to keep debt on a downward path while protecting social spending, and broad structural reforms to reduce the state footprint and level the playing field; it also says the agenda includes publishing a President-endorsed state ownership policy and an ambitious divestment plan.
evidence.source_locator: paragraph 9 and the SOE reforms section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: IMF staff report with specific program design and implementation commitments, though retrospective to the late-2022 package.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective description of the late-2022 program and implementation framework.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The program is the government's, not a private staff memo; it is attributable to Sisi's administration but still not a direct record of his personal decision-making.
contrary_evidence: The report frames these as commitments and mechanisms, not as completed outcomes inside 2022.

evidence.claim: The FY 2022/23 draft budget allocated EGP 302.2 billion to social protection, including support for Takaful and Karama, housing, and home-gas connection, while the ministry said the policy package was intended to keep poverty trending downward.
evidence.title: Gov’t allocates EGP 302 billion to support social welfare in the state’s FY 2022/2023 plan: Planning Minister
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Planning and Economic Development
evidence.excerpt: The FY 2022/23 draft budget allocated EGP 302.2 billion to social protection, including support for Takaful and Karama, housing, and home-gas connection, while the ministry said the policy package was intended to keep poverty trending downward.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry budget-planning announcement with named allocations and targets.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State budget planning under Sisi's presidency, but still a budget plan and target statement rather than proof of realized results.
contrary_evidence: The document itself treats the poverty figures as goals or expected direction rather than audited end-year outcomes.

evidence.claim: President Abdel Fattah El Sisi approved the State Ownership Policy Document, which was meant to define the state's relation with the private sector and expand private-sector participation in development projects, and the government said it would put the document into force immediately.
evidence.title: Sisi approves State Ownership Policy Document
evidence.excerpt: President Abdel Fattah El Sisi approved the State Ownership Policy Document, which was meant to define the state's relation with the private sector and expand private-sector participation in development projects, and the government said it would put the document into force immediately.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official announcement of a named presidential approval and its immediate policy effect.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable as a presidential approval, but still only a formal policy commitment rather than an implementation audit.
contrary_evidence: The announcement does not by itself show that the policy was enforced across state-owned and military-linked entities during 2022.

evidence.claim: A Saudi sovereign-wealth-fund unit bought minority stakes in four Egyptian listed companies for $1.3 billion, showing that the government's asset-sale and private-capital program had moved from announcement to execution in 2022.
evidence.title: Saudi Arabia’s $10 Billion Pledge to Egypt Delivers First Deals
evidence.excerpt: A Saudi sovereign-wealth-fund unit bought minority stakes in four Egyptian listed companies for $1.3 billion, showing that the government's asset-sale and private-capital program had moved from announcement to execution in 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-sourced Bloomberg reporting with a specific transaction, buyer, value, and target companies.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The transaction was executed by state-linked Egyptian entities under the government's program, not by Sisi personally, but it is strong evidence of ruler-attributable implementation.
contrary_evidence: It is a minority-stake sale in four firms, so it does not prove broader private-sector rebalancing on its own.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said foreign-exchange buffers had fallen sharply since March 2022, the Central Bank allowed depreciation and raised rates, the government announced social mitigation packages, growth was expected to slow to 4.5 percent in FY2022/23, and poverty could increase because inflation was eroding real incomes.
evidence.title: Egypt Economic Monitor, December 2022: Strengthening Resilience through Fiscal and Education Sectors Reforms
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said foreign-exchange buffers had fallen sharply since March 2022, the Central Bank allowed depreciation and raised rates, the government announced social mitigation packages, growth was expected to slow to 4.5 percent in FY2022/23, and poverty could increase because inflation was eroding real incomes.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent multilateral assessment summarizing contemporaneous policy responses and their likely effects.
evidence.ruler_attribution: These measures are attributable to the CBE and government under Sisi's administration, but the report also makes clear that external shocks materially constrained choices.
contrary_evidence: The same monitor notes that gas extractives, communications, agriculture, and construction were still performing relatively well, and FY2021/22 growth had rebounded strongly.

unresolved_gaps: No direct evidence of Sisi personally making a 2022 nuclear-safety, command-and-control, or crisis-escalation choice.
Concrete durable-conflict outcomes are thin beyond mediation and de-escalatory posture.
Exact chains of command and the effectiveness of pardon/reform mechanisms remain opaque.
There was no 2022 election, so contestability and transfer-rule evidence remains mostly structural rather than event-based.
Household-level distribution and implementation depth of the reform package are still thin.
Independent 2022 household outcome data are still thin, especially on whether transfers and pensions offset inflation.
There is no direct 2022 asset declaration, audit trail, procurement finding, or court judgment tying Sisi or close family to specific private gain from office.
Direct truthfulness/correction evidence from Sisi's own statements is still thin.
Direct evidence of Sisi's personal steering of tactical adjustments and durable outcome attribution remains limited.
